description:
In steady state, flows are specified. In dynamic mode, flows must be SOLVED from the pressure field, otherwise a valve closing changes nothing downstream and the simulator is not really transient.

SCOPE: a simultaneous pressure-flow network over the flowsheet graph, with the resistance of valves and pipes and the head of pumps and compressors, so that flow rate becomes a computed variable driven by pressure differences and inventory changes. This is what couples a valve stroke to a downstream response.

Relates to op-1z3o.5 (the steady-state sequential-modular solver) but is a different mathematical problem — simultaneous rather than sequential — so it deserves its own solve path.

Reference DWSIM dynamic mode for the formulation. Enum dispatch over element types, no trait objects.
title: refinery: pressure-flow network solve for dynamic mode

description:
Parent: op-841p. ON THE CRITICAL PATH for rung 1 step 1d and for all of rung 3.

THE PROBLEM. IAEA-TECDOC-1382 part 2 (OPEN tier, crates/kovan-literature/generated/markdown/open/iaea-tecdoc-1382-part2.md) line 189 is a bare caption, 'FIG. 4.10. HTR-10 core physics calculation model (see Table 4-3)'. Table 4-3 (lines 179-187) gives ONLY zone number -> carbon atom density -> natural boron atom density -> a one-line remark, for 83 zones. Core radius, conus angle, discharge-tube radius, cavity height and the axial coordinates of every zone boundary are ABSENT AS TEXT. The formal B1 definition subsection (4.1.2.1) is also missing from the markdown conversion - its body was absorbed into the Table 4-3 dump, gap at lines 170-198.

WHAT IS TEXTUALLY AVAILABLE (use, but it is not enough):
- Core radius 90 cm (line 1453); core diameter 180 cm (line 43); mean height 197 cm.
- Russia's FIG 4.20 axis labels survive as bare OCR'd numbers (lines 775-801): radial 90, 95.6, 108.6, 167.793, 190; axial 105, 114.7, 130, 171.698, 351.818, 388.764, 402, 430. KEY statement at line 799: Z = 351.818 cm corresponds to zero core height, i.e. the top of the conus. The pairing of these numbers to specific zone boundaries is NOT recoverable and must not be treated as authoritative.
- Control-rod channel 13 cm diameter at r = 102.1 cm; rod lower end 119.2 cm withdrawn, 394.2 cm inserted (lines 109, 111). Twenty helium channels 80 mm at r = 1446 mm, z = 1050-6100 mm (line 197).
- VTB's Griffin deck gives an outer bound: vacuum at sqrt(x^2+y^2) > 165.0, bottom z < 41, top z > 490 (reference-data/virtual_test_bed/htgr/htr10/steady/htr-10-critical.i:74, :80-81, :88-89).

THREE ROUTES, MAINTAINER TO CHOOSE:
1. Read the dimensions off Figure 4.10 in the PDF (crates/kovan-literature/open/reports/iaea-tecdoc-1382-part2.pdf) and record the digitisation as a documented processing step per DATA_POLICY.md.
2. Obtain Terry, W.K. (2005), 'Evaluation of the initial critical configuration of the HTR-10 pebble-bed reactor', INL/CON-05-00852 - the geometry source Choo and Xiao (2024) cite.
3. Obtain the VTB HTR-10 mesh from upstream, which encodes the geometry directly. NOTE it is NOT in this checkout - see the VTB correction bead.

USEFUL AND ALREADY PRESENT: Table 4-3's 83-zone homogenised atom densities (lines 179-187), Table 4-37's pebble-bed cell geometry (line 1089), and Table 4-38's explicit atom densities (line 1101) which the rung-1 example already consumes.

notes.author: fifad@Teddy-Thinkpad
notes.content:
MAINTAINER DECISION 2026-08-13: route 2 chosen -- obtain Terry, W.K. (2005), 'Evaluation of the initial critical configuration of the HTR-10 pebble-bed reactor', INL/CON-05-00852. Rationale: an authoritative text source with real numbers beats digitising a figure, and procurement runs in parallel with the cfmesh meshing work so it costs no critical-path time.

FALLBACK, only if it cannot be obtained: route 1, digitise FIG 4.10 from crates/kovan-literature/open/reports/iaea-tecdoc-1382-part2.pdf using kovan-digitise. If it comes to that: use the CLI (never read points off the figure by eye -- CLAUDE.md hard rule), supply axis references explicitly since there is no tick-label OCR, and note that an agent run can ONLY ever emit Unreviewed -- the maintainer marks it reviewed.

ON ARRIVAL: catalogue Terry 2005 into kovan-literature with its access tier decided from its own copyright page, per the 'ANY literature ingested OR USED goes into kovan' hard rule. Check the extracted metadata round-trips through 'kovan lit bibtex' before trusting it.

notes.author: fifad@Teddy-Thinkpad
notes.content:
PARTIALLY RESOLVED 2026-08-13. The maintainer supplied Terry et al. (2005), INL/CON-05-00852, obtained from https://www.osti.gov/servlets/purl/911178. Catalogued as PROPRIETARY (its first page says 'should not be cited or reproduced without permission of the author' -- OSTI hosting grants no redistribution rights, and the tier comes from the copyright page per DATA_POLICY.md). PDF at crates/kovan-literature/proprietary/reports/terry2005-htr10-benchmark-evaluation.pdf (gitignored).

DIMENSIONS RECORDED, with provenance, in docs/reactor-scoping/htr10-neutronics.md, new final section. Its Table 2 supplies the axial build this bead said was absent from the open text:
  Height of core cavity  221.818 cm
  Height of conus         36.946 cm
  Core radius 90 cm, loading height 123.06 cm
  Reflector OD 380 cm, height 610 cm
  Discharge tube r = 25 cm, height 610 cm
  Cold coolant channels 8.0 cm dia at r = 144.6 cm, height 405 cm
  Control-rod/irradiation channels 13 cm dia at r = 102.1 cm, height 450 cm
  KLAK 6 cm upper/lower, 88.2743 cm2 middle; hot gas duct D=30 cm L=100 cm
  Pebble packing fraction 0.61; upper-surface cone angle 19.5 deg

Also independently confirms packing fraction 0.61 for op-5c5r, and gives the 19.5 deg cone angle -- but Terry says that angle was CALCULATED by an INL DEM code and explicitly NOT measured, so it is a modelling assumption, not data.

STILL OPEN: the 83-zone R-Z boundaries of TECDOC Table 4-3 are NOT in this paper. Terry section 1 says it is a summary and directs the reader to the IRPhEP evaluation report itself (its ref [3]) for the detailed benchmark model. Obtaining THAT report is the remaining work here. Recommend keeping this bead open at P2 and retitling scope to the zone boundaries only.

Facts vs document: the numbers are recorded because facts are not copyrightable and Terry section 1 states all descriptive data came from published documents, mainly the two IAEA TECDOCs which this workspace already holds OPEN -- so they have an open provenance path. For publication, cite the IRPhEP report or the TECDOCs, NOT this preprint.

notes.author: fifad@Teddy-Thinkpad
notes.content:
CORRECTION 2026-08-13, superseding my previous comment on this bead. I claimed Terry does not contain the R-Z zone boundaries. That was WRONG. It was concluded from the extracted TEXT only (130 lines), which genuinely lacks them -- but the paper's FIGURES carry them: section 2 describes Fig. 2 as the simplified model, 'axisymmetric (the borings are homogenized in the zones where they are located)', which is exactly the R-Z zone map. Fig. 1 is the high-fidelity version.

They are RASTER: the PDF has 5 /Subtype /Image objects, all FlateDecode, and zero vector drawing operators, so coordinates are not exactly recoverable from the content stream. The figures must be DIGITISED with kovan-digitise (CLI, per the CLAUDE.md hard rule -- never read points off a figure by eye; only the maintainer may mark a dataset reviewed).

USEFUL SYNERGY: an engineering figure has no axes to calibrate against, but Terry's Table 2 gives exact known dimensions -- core radius 90 cm, reflector OD 380 cm, reflector height 610 cm -- which serve as explicit --x-ref/--y-ref pixel=value anchors. Table 2 sets the scale, Fig. 2 gives the boundaries.

BLOCKED ON TOOLING: kovan lit import cannot emit the figures. extract_assets() exists in the library (pdf_import.rs:70) but the CLI has no flag for it. Filed as its own bead.

ALSO STILL WORTH OBTAINING: ref [3], 'International Handbook of Evaluated Reactor Physics Benchmark Experiments', NEA/NSC/DOC(2006)1, OECD NEA (2006) -- Terry section 1 directs the reader there for the full benchmark model. Tabulated boundaries would beat digitised ones.

title: HTR-10 neutronics: obtain the R-Z zone geometry - it is not recoverable from the open text

acceptance_criteria: Sobol estimator reproduces the closed-form Ishigami indices within its sampling error; an additive linear model gives first-order indices summing to 1 and equal to the total indices; Sobol g-function checked for a strongly interacting case. Correlation measures checked against a known correlation matrix and a monotone non-linear transform (Spearman preserved, Pearson not). Methodology AND measured numbers with uncertainty and date recorded.
description:
Implement crates/raffles/src/sensitivity.rs. Sobol first-order S_i and total-effect S_Ti indices (with the Saltelli A-B-AB matrix construction, which belongs to the estimator), Pearson/Spearman correlation, partial correlation (PCC/PRCC), standardised regression coefficients (SRC/SRRC), plus the sample mean/variance/covariance they build on. All dimensionless: indices in [0,1], correlations in [-1,1].

Upstream: ravenframework/Models/PostProcessors/, ravenframework/Metrics/.

LICENCE WARNING: this is the area where RAVEN vendors third-party BSD code (AMSC — Univ. of Utah SCI Institute, 3-clause BSD; NGL — Carlos D. Correa, 2-clause BSD), in the topological-decomposition / Morse-Smale parts. Files derived from those need the BSD attribution header, NOT Apache-2.0. Check the upstream component before writing any header. See crates/raffles/NOTICE-RAVEN.

Enum dispatch — no Box<dyn>, no lifetimes.

NOT here: generating the design (samplers), surrogate construction.
title: raffles: sensitivity module

description:
FIXED 2026-08-13. RE-FILED after tracker data loss (see docs/kopitiam-issues/).

The op-ad6h defect existed in THREE places: outram-foam-basic-lib, tampines-steam-tables/src/openfoam_algorithms/openfoam_source/ode/, and outram-park-fork-coolprop/src/openfoam_algorithms/openfoam_source/. diff -r showed the two vendored trees differ only in doc wording and use-ordering.

Confirmed by demonstration, not inference. In BOTH trees Rosenbrock23::solve_step imports integrate_interval and normalize_error but NOT adaptive_step, so it duplicates the retry loop; the guard was proven load-bearing by deleting it and watching the tests fail with Err(StepSizeUnderflow) instead of Err(NonFiniteState).

SEVERITY NUANCE: the enum variant surfaced NO consumers in either crate -- OdeError appears only inside openfoam_source/ode/, and adaptive_step is called only by euler.rs and rkf45.rs. So here the defect was LATENT, a trap for the first consumer, unlike basic-lib where it was actively reachable.

Gates: tampines-steam-tables 955 passed / 0 failed / 13 ignored; outram-park-fork-coolprop 282 / 0 / 4; cargo check --workspace --lib --release clean.

RECOMMENDATION for op-xji, not acted on: delete both vendored ODE sub-trees and depend on outram-foam-basic-lib. One defect fixed three times is the concrete case op-xji describes, and the ODE sub-tree is the cheapest pilot because it has ZERO consumers -- removing it changes no behaviour and no public surface. Countervailing constraint documented in coolprop openfoam_algorithms/CLAUDE.md: the vendoring is deliberate so that crate depends only on uom and stays Android-buildable, whereas basic-lib pulls ndarray. Maintainer decision.
title: Two vendored openfoam_source ODE trees carried the same NaN-as-success defect (FIXED); de-duplication recommended
